cross_layer_patterns.name: Anisotropy & Scale Surprise
cross_layer_patterns.description: Isotropic theory matches anisotropic plasma (Alfvén); standard models fail for Perseus; vacuum assumption may fail for GW190728. All three reveal Layer 1↔2 boundary through scale mismatch.
cross_layer_patterns.layer_implication: Layer 1↔2 discriminator: when theory breaks, check scale/anisotropy assumptions
cross_layer_patterns.testable_prediction: Anisotropic systems will show systematic deviations from isotropic approximations at A_c > 30

cross_layer_patterns.name: Energy Hierarchy → A_c
cross_layer_patterns.description: A_c ≈ 2.5·log(E_max/E_min) + 16.1 (linear fit across 4 systems). Dark Matter system spans 79 orders of magnitude → highest A_c. This suggests A_c is fundamentally a renormalization group depth measure.
cross_layer_patterns.layer_implication: A_c measures RG flow depth, not just structural complexity
cross_layer_patterns.testable_prediction: Any physical system spanning N orders of magnitude in energy will have A_c proportional to N

cross_layer_patterns.name: Φ Inversion
cross_layer_patterns.description: Dark Matter system has Φ=0.463 > Perseus (0.25) despite larger scale. Because DM cloud ↔ BH ↔ GW form tightly coupled triple. Suggests Φ peaks at intermediate coupling, not maximal scale.
